items.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: one wide 16:9 2D pixel-art gameplay screenshot for an article about Eoul, a bright Korean folklore game world.
Primary request: Show the actual playable moment of a mythic ecological fishing simulator. The player reads surface wake, tug rhythm, and line strain, then chooses reel, slack, or rod angle. This must look like a game screen, not promotional key art.
Scene/backdrop: clear turquoise cove beside a small Korean island village, dark rocks, reeds, distant tiled roofs, late afternoon.
Subject: one fisher in practical hanbok on a small wooden pier, rod bent toward one large fish shadow under water. A single taut line. The fish wake curves toward a rock, with two short ripple pulses followed by one long pulse.
Composition/framing: mostly top-down 2D game camera. Bottom HUD has three large choices with icons: reel spool, open hand for slack, angled rod. Left HUD has signal rows: wake arrow, tug pattern as two short dots and one long dash, line strain at 64%. Right panel has locked post-catch icons: basket, open-water release, shared meal. Small weather icon and tide strip at top.
Style/medium: crisp handcrafted 16-bit pixel art, square pixels, readable sprites, limited teal-coral-cream palette, functional dark UI panels, polished Korean indie pixel game.
Lighting/mood: calm but tactile tension, bright readable water.
Text (verbatim): TUG, LINE 64, REEL, SLACK.
Constraints: real-time line tension control from incomplete signals is central. No fish health bar, combat, cards, inventory grid, logo, watermark, or poster composition. Opaque full-bleed landscape.
visual_qa: 물결 방향, 두 번의 짧은 입질과 한 번의 긴 입질, LINE 64%를 각각 확인
REEL, SLACK, 낚싯대 각도 세 입력과 잠긴 잡은 뒤 선택 세 항목 확인
체력바·전투·카드 없이 줄 장력이 중심인 실제 플레이 화면 확인

items.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: one wide 16:9 2D pixel-art gameplay screenshot for an article about Eoul, a bright Korean folklore game world.
Primary request: Show the actual playable editor of a freehand creative village sandbox. Distinct ink tools turn player strokes into a living Korean alley: road-ink lines become paths, wall-ink lines become walls, road-road crossings become plazas, road-wall crossings become gates, closed loops become courtyards, and contextual dots become a tree inside a courtyard or a lamp beside a road. Preview every result before placement. The pleasure is drawing and watching residents use it, not solving a fixed puzzle.
Scene/backdrop: warm rice-paper planning space seamlessly turning into a colorful top-down hanok neighborhood.
Subject: visible brush cursor finishing one previewed road-ink line. A wall-ink line crosses it at a gate. One closed loop is a courtyard with a tree dot. A road-side dot is a lamp. Exactly three tiny residents walk, rest, and turn through the built space.
Composition/framing: top-down actual game view. Left two-thirds show the evolving neighborhood. Right compact palette clearly separates road ink, wall ink, courtyard loop, and contextual dot. Bottom has undo, redo, daylight preview and camera icons. Resident request uses only three icons: sunrise, tree, quiet. Show a soft walking-path preview.
Style/medium: crisp hand-placed 16-bit pixel art, square pixels, cream paper, charcoal ink, terracotta, jade, lantern amber, polished functional editor UI.
Lighting/mood: peaceful morning creation.
Text (verbatim): INK 72, UNDO.
Constraints: no combat, currency, production, waves, tile-grid puzzle, exact target silhouette, management spreadsheet, large title, logo, watermark, or key art. Opaque full-bleed landscape.
visual_qa: 길 획, 담, 안마당, 나무와 등불의 서로 다른 팔레트와 반투명 미리보기 확인
정확히 세 주민의 걷기·앉기·이동 경로와 해·나무·조용함 부탁 아이콘 확인
